brief: Savone frames the week as open to two readings: still an AI unwind, or a broader growth scare. Nvidia beat revenue by about $7B and guided about $5B ahead, yet shares fell 22.7% as export controls, financing and doubts about AI-investment returns drove selling beyond Technology. Macro data (retail sales beat, low jobless claims, a 19-month high in job postings) signaled resilience even as 2-year yields fell 24bps, copper fell 9.9% and oil fell 5.8%, with the S&P 500's forward P/E falling to 16.5x. Hawkish Fedspeak evoked 2018: markets price about 62bps of hikes over 10 months, and Morgan Stanley's Metli argues 2018 showed it was pricing the pivot, not the pivot itself, that stopped the selloff. Asia (Taiwan -6.2%, Korea -5.2%, Japan -5.1%) and Europe (worst week since Liberation Day, a flight into Staples) extended the selloff; corporates sound more constructive than investors. Funds kept de-grossing, pushing US long/short net leverage to 41%, near COVID and Liberation Day lows. The remainder rounds up dozens of individual bank research calls across sectors, regions and asset classes.
